detail.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency
detail.summary: Recent advances indicate that foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (separating justification from cognition), structured, teacher-guided self-correction, and probabilistic quantification of uncertainty. PCFG-derived metrics and Brier scores allow systems to detect when their confidence (an implicit assumption of correctness) fails to match empirical outcome distributions.
detail.reason: Incorporating quantitative uncertainty and coverage guarantees as a foundational challenge mechanism.

detail.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency
detail.summary: Foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (decoupling cognition from control) and the deliberate inclusion of dissonance to prevent premature closure on unverified truths. CD-AI frameworks specifically operationalize this doubt.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate CD-AI concepts as a methodology for axiom testing.

detail.title: Flow-State as an Emergent Preference
detail.summary: Evidence suggests that users have a persistent, stable preference for 'flow' states. AI systems that prioritize this preference must minimize disruptive interventions, using control loops to verify whether an intervention actually supports or hinders the user's flow.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate control-loop verification as a mechanism for validating user flow preferences.
